You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual Harness State

Local continual harness entries belong to this Prime Agent session. Global continual harness entries persist across Prime Agent sessions.
The continual harness entries below are compact summaries, not full descriptions. Use them as routing/context hints; inspect or refine the underlying continual harness entry only when detail matters.
Default to local continual harness refinement for current task progress, temporary blockers, and session coordination. Use global continual harness refinement only for stable cross-session lessons, durable user preferences, reusable skills/subagents, or explicitly project-qualified facts.
Use these continual harness prompt notes, memories, skills, and subagent specs when they are relevant. The base system prompt is immutable; prompt entries below are supplemental notes only.

When to call `await refine.run()`: after a repeated failure, a reusable tactic emerges, a repeated delegation role should become a subagent spec, a repeated procedure should become a skill, a durable fact/preference should become a memory, a narrow behavioral policy should become a prompt addendum, a user corrects behavior that should persist locally or globally, validation shows a continual harness entry is wrong, or a skill/subagent/memory/prompt note should be created, updated, deleted, or rolled back. Keep `await refine.run()` continual harness edits small and evidence-backed.

Call contract: read each installed Python skill's SKILL.md and call its documented module function in the Python REPL; do not assume a `.run` entrypoint. Use `<skill_import> ...` in shell when a CLI exists. Continual harness skill entries are Python REPL skills with an explicit Python `reference` and `arguments` contract. Spawn a continual harness subagent spec by composing a concise task prompt and calling `handle = await rlm.spawn('sub-task', name='worker')`; admission returns immediately with `rlm_child_id`, `name`, `session_dir`, and `model`, never the child's answer. Results arrive only through explicit `agent_message` replies or files; children reply with `await agent_message.send(message, receiver_role='parent')`. Use `await rlm.list_subagents()` to recover direct child handles and `await agent_message.send(..., receiver_role='child', receiver_name=handle.name)` for follow-ups. Do not invent wrappers such as `call_skill(...)`, `run_subagent(...)`, or named subagent registries.

Check demos for differing outpu'), ('arc_task_d4c70c99_mark_matching_colors_across_separator', 'ARC task-d4c70c99: mark matching colors across separator', 'For recurring task-d4c70c99, the grid has two equal-sized panels separated by a single uniform divider (vertical or horizontal). Example: demo input background 5 with object 4 became 4 on former background cells and 0 on former 4 cells; for analogous test background 5/object 9, output 9 where input was 5 and 0 where input was 9. Preserve dimensions; no shape-based filling.'), ('arc_task_9a9f2d3f_stamp_marker_shape_onto_matching_zeros', 'ARC task-9a9f2d3f: stamp marker shape onto matching zeros', 'For task-9a9f2d3f, the input is a binary grid (typically 0 plus another color) with a small pattern in a third marker color. Slide this mask over every in-bounds location of the original grid; whenever every occupied mask position contains 0, recolor those occupied positions to the marker color. Take the union of all hits, preserving all other cells and the original marker. Do not require the mask’s blank positions to match anything. Demo validated this: on one fragmented 8 row, cells strictly right of its rightmost 8 became 1; the repeated row already filled with 8s stayed unchanged. Test solved by turning the 0 tail to 1 on two partial horizontal 8 rows.'), ('arc_rule_slide_object_toward_color_2_line_and_mark_far_side', 'ARC rule: slide object toward color-2 line and mark far side', "For ARC grids with background 4, a full straight line of color 2, and a separate non-background object, preserve and slide the object along the perpendicular axis toward the color-2 line until it is directly adjacent to that line. Each compartment has a uniform background color and sparse pixels of another color. Produce a smaller grid with one cell per compartment: preserve the input background color for compartments with zero or one marker pixel; use color 1 for any compartment containing more than one marker pixel. Demos: panels with two markers map to 1; panels with a single marker or none map to panel background. Count markers per compartment; adjacency/shape does not matter.'), ('arc_task_4b1f4f06_shifted_edge_rails_project_marker_rays', 'ARC task-4b1f4f06: shifted edge rails project marker rays', "For recurring ARC task-4b1f4f06, two equal-color rail segments lie on opposite parallel grid edges, shifted along the edge direction; isolated markers are in the rail color (or another foreground color) on one active rail's coordinate range. Extend a source-side ray from the marker toward its own edge rail, in the marker's original color, stopping before the rail. Translate its coordinate along the rail axis by d and draw a full perpendicular line across the grid at that translated coordinate in the marker col"), ('arc_rule_overlap_aligned_panels_into_color_2', 'ARC rule: overlap aligned panels into color 2', 'For ARC grids split into two equal-sized panels by a uniform one-cell divider row or column, compare aligned cells across panels. Output a grid the size of one panel, with color 2 wherever both corresponding input cells are nonzero, and 0 elsewhere. Ignore the divider and original foreground colors. This applies whether either panel is sparse or dense; it was demonstrated across horizontal and vertical splits. Practical check: for a vertical split, align each left-panel column with the same-index right-panel column; for a horizontal split, align rows. Ensure every overlap is included (a missed single overlap caused one wrong submission on tas'), ('arc_reflection_tiling_3_high_by_2_wide', 'ARC reflection tiling: 3 high by 2 wide', 'For ARC tasks that transform an input grid into a 3H x 2W output by mirror tiling, construct each output row from a horizontal reflection of the corresponding input row followed by the original row. Vertically tile the input as [vertical_flip(input), input, vertical_flip(input)]. Equivalently output block rows are top vertical-flipped input, middle original input, bottom vertical-flipped input; each block has columns [horizontal_flip(input), input]. This matches task-30861639: demo 1 input 8x6 -> output 24x12; demo 2 input 1x5 -> output 3x10. Uniform 2x3 test consequently becomes 6x6 all 2s. For H=1, vertical flips are identical. Current solv'), ('arc_task_7acf9041_expand_grid_into_four_rotations', 'ARC task-7acf9041: expand grid into four rotations', 'For recurring task-7acf9041, take the square input grid A (N×N) and make a 2N×2N output arranged as four rotated copies: top-left A unchanged; top-right A rotated 90° clockwise; bottom-left A rotated 90° counterclockwise; bottom-right A rotated 180°. Equivalently output blocks [[A, rot90(A, clockwise)], [rot90(A, counterclockwise), rot180(A)]]. Preserve all cell colors. Demonstrations: 15×15→30×30 and 13×13→26×26 confirmed the block arrangement; a 10×10 test was solved correctly with this rule.'), ('arc_recolor_sparse_color_5_marks_with_the_background_color', 'ARC: recolor sparse color-5 marks with the background color', 'For ARC grids with a mostly uniform background color B and scattered cells of color 5, demonstrations show a simple palette conversion preserving positions: change every background B cell to 0, and every scattered 5 cell to B. Confirmed examples: B=2, marks=5 -> 0/2; B=1, marks=5 -> 0/1; B=6, marks=5 -> 0/6. Do not assume marks always become color 2; they become the original background color. A separate demo with a uniform 5 background and one 9 outlier mapped background 5->9 and outlier9->0, so that rare-outlier case differs; infer from examples and use the common sparse-5 pattern when applicable.'), ('arc_complete_sparse_periodic_row_diagonal_patterns', 'ARC: complete sparse periodic row/diagonal patterns', 'For ARC grids containing a partial periodic pattern with zeros as missing/background cells, infer the shortest period consistent with the visible nonzero pattern and repeat it to fill the grid. Detect the repeating direction/coordinate: examples included a 5x5 diagonal motif where cell color depended on (column-row) modulo 4, and a horizontal-stripe 10x10 input with known consecutive rows [9,1,4,6,7,6] at rows 2–7; repeating that six-row motif vertically gave rows [7,6,9,1,4,6,7,6,9,1] and solved the task. A sparse 25x25 stripe demo exposed an 8-row period [8,2,8,9,7,4,7,1], inferred as the smallest period consistent with the visible row samp'), ('arc_fill_gaps_between_alternating_row_marks_with_2', 'ARC: fill gaps between alternating row marks with 2', 'For ARC grids containing horizontal runs of alternating marker/background cells, insert color 2 in each single background cell between horizontally adjacent marker cells, leaving endpoints and all other cells unchanged.
